subject: Sentinel discovery: integration plan, auth choices, embeddings + prompt governance
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@sentinel.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@sentinel.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Intro call follow-up + a few clarifying questions

Thanks for the call today — good overview. A couple items we need clarified so our infra team can sign off: 

1) SDK footprint and sample auth flow (we run a mix of service-to-service and browser-initiated requests)
2) How do you recommend routing between hosted vs dedicated models for low-latency inference across our US/EU regions?
3) We plan to use embeddings + reranker for search ranking; curious about your guidance on vector size, storage, and update frequency for near-real-time content.

Also asked about the safety of system prompts — we need a short version of your prompt governance (versioning, red-team cadence, injection mitigations) to include in our security questionnaire.

Can someone from your infra team share a minimal SDK sample and an auth recommendation?

Thanks,
Alex
Head of ML Platform | Sentinel.ai

(Attachment: product-one-pager.pdf)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@sentinel.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Intro call follow-up + a few clarifying questions

Alex — great questions, glad we had the sync. High-level answers below; Dev and Marissa are looped to provide artifacts and timelines. I put concrete next steps at the bottom.

SDK & auth
- We’ll provide a lean SDK (Node + Java) that supports both API-key and mTLS+token-exchange flows. For browser-initiated calls we recommend a short-lived token broker (your backend mints ephemeral tokens) — avoids embedding long-lived keys in the client.
- We’ll attach an example auth flow (service-to-service with KMS-stored keys + optional OIDC) in the sample bundle.

Routing & latency
- Recommend policy-based routing: prefer dedicated capacity in-region for low-p99 latency; fallback to hosted variants in nearest region. Routing is policy-driven and can be set per route/model. We’ll include a sample routing policy for your EU/US split.

Embeddings + reranker
- Default vector dims: 1024 for semantic search with our curated open models; can scale down to 768 for cost.
- Store vectors in your vector DB of choice; we provide stable hashing for upserts to avoid duplicate embeddings. For near-real-time updates we recommend micro-batching at 30–60s with incremental upserts.

Prompt governance (summary)
- Version prompts with a semver-like tag: prompt_v1.0.0, prompt_v1.1.0 (minor tweaks), prompt_v1.1.1 (safety patches).
- Keep canonical prompt artifacts in your repo/Drive and reference a checksum in the model request metadata.
- Mitigations: input sanitization, explicit system message separators, and a runtime prompt-safety filter that rejects or neutralizes suspicious tokens/patterns.
- Red-team cadence: lightweight weekly unit tests on synthetic injections + monthly larger red-team runs that include adversarial prompts and context poisoning scenarios.

Next steps (what we’ll deliver by Wed):
- Dev: SDK sample + auth flow (Node + Java) (see attachment: sdk-auth-sample.tar.gz)
- Marissa: updated pricing note for mixed hosted/dedicated routing and a sample routing policy
- Dylan: short prompt-governance one-pager + prompt-versioning-proposal.md

If this looks good I’ll send a short Statement of Work outline to match the deliverables.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

(Attachment: MVP-integration-checklist.xlsx)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@sentinel.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: SDK samples + auth patterns (attached)

Alex — attaching the SDK samples and a README for the auth patterns. Highlights: 

- browser-token-broker.md: pattern for minting ephemeral tokens from your backend using OIDC or API-key exchange.
- svc-to-svc.md: mTLS + short-lived JWT flow with KMS signing (recommended for Dedicated).
- routing-examples.json: example policy that sends low-latency routes to dedicated pools and falls back to hosted (includes pseudo-policy snippets).

Prompt-safety hooks are included as a small middleware (prompt_safety.py) you can run pre-send; it flags likely prompt-injection patterns and enforces the system-message separator. For production we recommend the runtime filter + periodic red-team runs.

I’ve also included a tiny script to produce embeddings in 1024 dims and chunking recommendations for content updates.

Let me know if you want a quick 30m walkthrough — happy to demo the broker flow.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Senior Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference

(Attachments: sdk-auth-sample.tar.gz, browser-token-broker.md, routing-examples.json)

From: Priya Sharma <priya@sentinel.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@sentinel.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro call follow-up + a few clarifying questions

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple quick clarifications before we schedule the security review: 

- For prompt-versioning: do you store the canonical prompts on Redwood side or do you expect us to store them and just pass a checksum? We prefer keeping canonical copies internally for audit.
- Red-team: can you share a short sample report from a previous monthly run (sanitized) so our security team can see the scope?

Also interested in a 30m demo of the token-broker flow this week if Dev is available.

—Priya
Director, Engineering | Sentinel.ai

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@sentinel.ai>, Alex Chen <alex@sentinel.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Intro call follow-up + a few clarifying questions

Priya — quick answers and action items: 

- Canonical prompts: we support both models. For auditability we recommend you store canonical copies internally and pass a checksum in requests. Redwood can also keep a copy if you’d like (we’ll store with strict ACLs and retention policies).
- Red-team sample: I’ll send a sanitized extract from a recent red-team engagement this afternoon.
- Demo: Dev — feel free to propose 30min slots today (I can join) — please include a short runbook for the token-broker demo.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Dev: propose 2x 30m demo slots + runbook (today EOD)
- Dylan: send sanitized red-team extract + prompt-versioning-proposal.md (today EOD)
- Marissa: follow-up pricing + SOW outline (Thu EOD)

If all good I’ll also open a HubSpot task and draft a one-page SOW to align timelines.

Thanks,
Dylan
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

(Attachment: prompt-versioning-proposal.md)
